This page sets out what you do in the independent format, and where. The [background page](../../background.qmd) presents the original study, the SCORE replication and the five reanalyses of the robustness study of SCORE [Multi100\; @AczelEtAl2026InvestigatingAnalyticalRobustness], and it is the place to start if you have not read it. The route takes all five tasks, and you do them in the workspace, which stage 1 installs and which you open in your IDE (Positron, RStudio, VS Code, etc.). The [browser lab](../../lab.qmd), a page of this site on which R runs inside your browser, holds every task as well, with hints and worked solutions, and it carries the work if your installation fails. Stage 1 takes Task 1, stage 3 Tasks 2 and 3, and stage 4 Tasks 4 and 5. Sending your results to the class chart is optional, and the helpers of Tasks 4 and 5 work exactly as they do in class.

### Your own project

Stage 5 asks a question beyond the claim, one that the data of the case study support, and fixes its preregistration with a date that someone else can check before anything in it runs. The page of [stage 5](stage-5.qmd) lists the projects that the case study supports.

## Links

The tools of the route:

- [Setup](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/setup.html) – installing R, Quarto and an IDE, and running the setup check of the workspace.
- [Setup help](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/help.html) – the problems that other participants have met, and what to do about each.
- [The workspace](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds-housing-workspace/) – the report of the workspace as it renders, with the output of every chunk under its code.
- [Browser lab](../../lab.qmd) – the whole exercise and its data in a browser tab, with hints and worked solutions.
- [Slides](../day/slides.qmd) – the deck of the day format, which the stages use, with the speaker notes of every slide.
